title: SimdQuickHeap variants A1 to A9: factorial analysis
intro: Goal: measure the effect of each SimdQuickHeap variant flag and find the best combination, separately for C++ and for Rust. The languages are never compared with each other. Each cell is the change in median time per operation when the term is on, as a 95% interval over passes. A screening design (32 runs, resolution IV) covered all nine flags plus a dummy bit that no code reads. A follow-up half fraction (32 runs, resolution VI) covered the six flags worth keeping. A sequential confirmation run tested the predicted best combinations against Opts 0.

sections.heading: C++ screening, 2^(10-5)
sections.text: Main effects and two-factor alias chains. The dummy row is the noise floor from code layout alone. This run predates commit c0b322d, which sorts C++ layers of 21 to 32 keys with Rust std's network sort instead of insertion sort, so its A7 row understates A7.

sections.heading: C++ follow-up, 2^(6-1) on A1 A2 A4 A5 A6 A7
sections.text: A3, A8 and A9 held off. Every two-factor interaction is clear of other two-factor interactions. Measured after commit c0b322d. Before it, C++ sorted 21 to 32 key layers with insertion sort and A7 measured −8.3% overall instead of −16.8%.

sections.heading: Rust follow-up, 2^(6-1) on A1 A2 A4 A5 A6 A7
C++ predicted best combinations
sections.text: Main effects plus two-factor interactions from the follow-up, all 64 combinations against all off, best 10 shown.

sections.heading: C++ confirmation, measured against Opts 0
sections.text: Seven sequential passes on CPU 3, nine Opts values in a shuffled order per pass, measured after commit c0b322d. Opts 203 was not measured in the follow-up. It measured −25.1% [−25.2, −25.0] against a predicted −25.1%. Paired across passes, adding A4 to A1+A2+A6+A7 changes the overall time by −0.5% [−0.9, +0.0], adding A3 by +0.7% [+0.2, +1.2], and adding A5 by +1.6% [+1.3, +2.0] (PushDecr +15.7%). Before the fix, Opts 203 measured −20.8%.

sections.heading: Rust confirmation, measured against Opts 0
sections.text: Seven sequential passes on CPU 5. Opts 217 was not measured in the follow-up. It measured −29.8% [−30.3, −29.3] against a predicted −30.2%. Paired across passes, adding A5 to A1+A4+A6+A7 changes the overall time by −0.7% [−1.7, +0.4], with Monotone −3.5%, HeapSort −4.6% and PushDecr +7.3%. Adding A2 to A1+A4+A5+A6+A7 costs +0.6%.
